result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder, whatever follows. That covers a plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/` and `mock-größe/`.

In `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/TestConventions.java` I replaced the two mock rules with one: `.*/(__)?mock[^/]*/.*`. The old ones only allowed ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-` and space, and required at least one character after `mock`.

I did not add new tests or check the listed cases (`mock/`, `mock.data/`, `remock/`, Windows paths) against the new pattern. `SourceFileFilter` already matches Windows-style paths by converting backslashes to `/`, so I expect them to work too. The run of tests matching `*Convention*` in `codeanalyzer` produced no failures, but I didn't confirm how many tests that pattern actually ran.

By reading the pattern, `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/` and files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` stay out, because the match is one whole folder name that starts with `mock`. The folders that were test before (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`) still match.
